issues.detail: 'feed'→'수유' narrows to breastfeeding: '아이에게 밥을 먹이다' passes though English bans feed. 'cook'→'요리' lets the synonym '조리' through.
Prompt URL 'Raymond_III,_Count_of_Tripoli' contains an ASCII comma; an answer that cites the source URL fails no_comma. Same in English.
The mandatory repeat already contains '인턴' and '성장', so keywords:existence passes even if the limerick omits them. Same in English (intern/grow).
Keyword is the inflected form '대답했다', not a stem; a fairy tale in -습니다 style writing '대답했습니다' fails. Rule 3 wants a stem such as '대답했'.

prompt_to_repeat contains '쉼표(,)를', so the required verbatim repeat puts an ASCII comma in the response; strict no_comma always fails. English repeat span has no comma. Loose passes only via first-line removal.
'have'→'영향' bans the content noun 'effect' rather than the verb 'have'; a different lexical restriction than the English.
'ours'→'우리' also bans '우리의' (our); English 'ours' does not match 'Our results', so the Korean constraint is broader.
Prompt requires '목표' but kwargs check only '지표' and '관리'; an answer omitting '목표' passes. English kwargs likewise omit 'objective'.
Latin-script 'IceFrog'/'Blizzard' and spaced '아이스 프로그' escape the forbidden match, so an answer naming them passes; kwargs carry only the Hangul forms.
